title: Edge cache reconciliation after weighted shift — retro & runbook draft
body:
Summary:

This doc captures the post-incident notes and an initial runbook draft for the edge-cache reconciliation problem we hit during the 2025-02-14 weighted egress shift to us-west-2. The incident surface was large: a class of requests experienced increased 503s and stale results in the first 20 minutes of the shift. Root cause, short version: inconsistent cache priming and TTL skew across edge clusters + a subtle key-hash mismatch introduced by an outbound header rewrite in the downstream origin that only exists in eu-west-1 proxies. That mismatch only surfaced once traffic weight crossed ~30% to us-west-2 and cache-hit amplification assumptions changed.

Impact: 
- 15–25% increased 5xx rate for requests with dynamic partial responses (inference responses with streaming attachments) for ~18 minutes.
- Observed p95 token latency increase from 220ms -> 480ms for affected route.
- Some user requests returned stale inference results (TTL skew) for up to 10 minutes until caches rewarmed.
- No customer data exfiltration; no SLA breach after final mitigation.

Timeline (local TZ):
- 09:02 — Begin weighted shift: us-west-2 weight 10% -> 35% over 15m (automation).
- 09:08 — First alert: SLO error budget burn for route /v1/generate (ops-alerts, p95 latency and 5xx).
- 09:11 — Oncall (Marcus) opens incident, pins shift automation.
- 09:13 — Quick triage: spike concentrated on stateful routes with caching headers. Cache-hit-rate drop in us-west-2 observed.
- 09:16 — Teams: SRE, Platform Eng (Claire), Serving Runtime oncall pulled in.
- 09:20 — Mitigation attempt: reduce us-west-2 weight to 20% (manual rollback step).
- 09:24 — 5xx rate continues; further investigation shows eu-west-1 proxies returning origin-modified keys -> misses in us-west-2 priming.
- 09:28 — Emergency CDN-level bypass for affected prefix implemented (edge TTL set to 0 for prefix /gen-stream/*) to force origin re-eval for critical requests.
- 09:35 — Stable 5xx rate returned to baseline, latency recovering by 09:50 as caches re-primed.

Technical analysis (deeper):
- Cache key pipeline: client-id + request-signature + accept-encoding -> hashed-key. eu-west-1 had a header rewrite for X-Client-Locale to support region-specific de-chunking. That rewrite changed the request-signature component in a way that was not normalized by our key canonicalizer (we assumed header rewrites only appended metadata, not mutate signature-relevant headers).
- Key variance: us-west-2 primed cache using the canonicalized key (new routing path) but eu-west-1 primed using the mutated key. When traffic weight increased, some clients got hits from eu-west-1 path and some from us-west-2 path; since keys diverged, hit rates dropped and origin load spiked leading to transient 5xx from origin throttles.
- TTL skew: origin-side TTLs were configured differently per region (legacy config in eu-west-1 had a 5m TTL, us-west-2 had 90s). This caused stale content to linger for eu-west-1-primed entries after we reduced edge TTL to 0 (we didn't invalidate all region-local caches).
- Race condition: the initial automation increased weight before automated warm-priming could fully complete the prioritized prefixes. The priming job was triggered but rate-limited and queued behind lower-priority background priming; net effect: cache population lag.

Immediate corrective actions we took: 
- Rollback partial (weight -> 20%) to limit exposure.
- Force-origin revalidation for critical prefixes using CDN control plane (set edge TTL -> 0 and purge for small prefix set).
- Manual sync: ran sync-edge-cache script (ops/tools) to replay recent production traces into us-west-2 priming pipeline with higher concurrency (bumped from 10->60 concurrent workers).
- Hotfix to canonicalizer: applied temporary normalization for X-Client-Locale to ignore it in signature composition (hotpatch in platform-proxy config, rolled to canary then full).

What went well: 
- Detection was quick due to p95 latency SLO alerts + route-level cache-hit dashboards.
- Cross-team comms were fast — Slack bridge + incident channel created within 3m.
- Automation allowed partial rollback quickly; manual adjustments were straightforward.

What could be improved / root causes to address: 
1) Configuration drift across edge regions (TTL, priming priority, header rewrite rules).
2) Cache key normalization assumptions not codified; too many implicit invariants.
3) Priming orchestration: prioritization and backpressure for warm-priming jobs is weak; default job priority allowed low-value priming to block critical prefixes.

Runbook draft: Edge Cache Reconciliation (for weighted routing changes)
Scope: for operators performing weighted traffic shifts or region failovers that rely on multi-region edge caches and prefix priming.
Status: draft — needs automation owners to validate commands and test in staging.

Operator checklist (pre-shift):
- Ensure global-config parity: run ./infra/scripts/check-edge-config --regions eu-west-1,us-west-2 and confirm TTLs and header-rewrite rules are identical for affected prefixes.
- Confirm priming queue status: /ops/priming/status -> no long-running low-priority backlog. If backlog > 5 mins for critical prefix, defer shift.
- Run dry-run priming for critical prefixes: ./ops/priming/run --prefix /gen-stream --target us-west-2 --concurrency 30 --dry-run -> verify estimated time < planned window.
- Verify key canonicalizer rules: ./infra/tools/key-canon --diff-configs eu-west-1 us-west-2 -> expect zero diffs for signature-relevant headers.
- Monitor baseline metrics: cache-hit-rate, origin-5xx-rate, p95 latency per-region for the last 30m.

Mitigation sequence (during incidents):
1) Pause or reduce weighted shift immediately to a safe level (operator knob documented: routing/weighted-shift -> set weight).
2) If 5xx or hit-rate degradation observed, trigger CDN edge revalidation for affected prefixes (edge TTL->0) for that specific prefix scope; do NOT global purge unless confirmed.
3) Run sync-edge-cache with targeted trace replay: ./ops/sync-edge-cache --prefixes /gen-stream,/embeds --from-trace last-15m --target-region us-west-2 --workers 50. Watch queue length.
4) If header mismatch suspected: apply temporary canonicalizer override (ops/config-hotpatch) to ignore non-signature headers OR roll back region-specific header rewrite.
5) If origin throttling persists: scale origin pool or reduce throughput by applying short-client-rate-limits on the problematic route until caches stabilize.

Verification checks (post mitigation):
- cache-hit-rate(us-west-2) >= 80% for prefix within 12 minutes.
- origin-5xx-rate for route normalized to baseline by 20 minutes.
- p95 latency returned within 1.2x baseline within 30 minutes.

Automation & tooling notes (TODOs):
- Add a pre-shift gating check into the weighted-shift automation: fail the shift if priming-estimate > planned window OR if key-canon diffs != 0. (Owner: Platform Eng — Claire Ho)
- Improve priming job QoS: ensure critical prefix jobs preempt background priming (Owner: infra-priming team — Ethan Chu).
- Create a canary test that sends identical tracer requests across regions to validate canonicalization end-to-end before full weighting (Owner: SRE).
- Extend telemetry: emit cache-key-hash histogram per region for top 50 prefixes to detect divergence quickly (Owner: Observability team).

Postmortem action items (owner — due):
- SRE: add automated pre-shift check to routing automation (Claire Ho) — due 2025-03-14.
- Platform: collapse header-rewrite variants; create a single canonicalizer rule set referenced by all proxies (Priya Desai) — due 2025-03-07.
- Infra-priming: implement priority queue and preemption for priming jobs (Ethan Chu) — due 2025-04-01.
- Observability: dashboard tile for cache-key divergence signals and per-region TTL fingerprints (Marcus Lee) — due 2025-03-10.
- Runbook: finalize commands and add playbook to runbook repo + verify in staging (Nora Kim) — due 2025-03-05.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we centralize TTL configs? Pros: fewer drift bugs. Cons: reduces region-specific tuning for latency. Tradeoff proposal: centralize critical-prefix TTLs, allow per-region tuning for non-critical static assets.
- How aggressive should priming replays be? We increased workers x6 in-incident; that itself risks origin overload. Need a feedback-driven priming algorithm that monitors origin 5xx and slows down.
- Do we need a global key canonicalizer service so proxies only consult a single source of truth? This would eliminate config drift but adds a dependency for request path.

Testing & drill plan:
- Add a staging exercise: simulate 40% weight shift with priming disabled and verify alerts, and then test with prioritized priming enabled. Capture timings. (Target: run in staging every 2 weeks for next 3 months.)
- Chaos test: randomly rewrite a non-critical header in one region's proxy and ensure key-canon detects divergence within 1 minute.

Notes to operators (quick cheat sheet):
- Useful commands: 
  - ops/priming/status -> shows queue times and prefix priorities 
  - ops/sync-edge-cache --help -> replay traces for priming 
  - infra/tools/key-canon --diff-configs R1 R2 -> show header diffs 
  - cdnctl set-ttl --prefix /gen-stream --ttl 0 --regions us-west-2 -> set edge TTL for prefix
  - cdnctl purge --prefix /gen-stream --regions us-west-2 -> careful: small scope only

Retrospective notes (feelings / soft takeaways):
- Operators felt the runbook lacked a single source-of-truth; too many small ad-hoc scripts were assembled. Consolidation will reduce cognitive overhead.
- The priming system's default batch behavior needs clearer SLAs. We tolerated long priming times because priming is cheap historically; in weighted shifts it is not.

Appendix — quick incident logs/snippets:
- Observability query used to detect divergence:
  - sum by (region) (rate(edge_cache_miss_total{prefix="/gen-stream"}[1m])) / sum by(region) (rate(requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[1m]))
- Example hotpatch command (ops-only):
  - kubectl -n platform-proxy exec -it canary-proxy -- /bin/sh -c \"apply-canon-rule "X-Client-Locale" ignore\"
- Sync script invocation (we used this during the incident):
  - ./ops/sync-edge-cache --prefixes /gen-stream --from-trace /traces/2025-02-14/09-00-09-30.log --target-region us-west-2 --workers 50 --dry-run=false

Final thought:
This incident highlights that weighted routing is a systemic coordination problem: routing automation, priming, canonicalization, and region config parity all need stronger guardrails. The proposed runbook and action items above aim to add those guardrails in low-friction ways (pre-shift gates, prioritized priming, canonicalizer diffs, and observability).

Draft status: request reviewers from Platform Eng + Observability + Serving Runtime. Please comment inline.

-- Nora (oncall)
